card_title: Same molecule, a very different idea
card_summary: Why a tiny dose of a decades-old medicine is a different conversation from the standard one.
headline: Same molecule. A *very* different idea.
lede: Low-dose naltrexone uses a sliver of the standard dose. Follow one dose through the body to see why researchers think the size changes what it does, and where the open questions are.
notice_intro: Every member is different. This is what studies have measured, not a promise.

notice_items.notice_text: Some people notice vivid dreams or lighter sleep early on. In small studies these were mostly mild and passed.
Studies have followed LDN for 8 to 12 weeks. Your clinician will tell you when to check in on how it's going.
Your clinician may adjust your strength or the time of day you take it. Tell them about any sleep changes.

cautions_intro: Your clinician screens for these during your intake. Read them anyway.

not_for_you_if.item_text: You take any opioid, including prescription pain medicine, methadone or buprenorphine. Naltrexone blocks opioids and can bring on withdrawal.
You have acute hepatitis or liver failure. The naltrexone label lists both as reasons not to use it.

what_to_watch.item_text: Sleep changes or vivid dreams, especially in the first weeks.
Nausea, especially in the first few nights.
If you might need opioid pain relief, for example before a procedure, tell your clinician and care team that you take naltrexone.

cadence_intro: Your plan as it's set up today.
cta_note: A licensed clinician reviews your health history and decides whether LDN is appropriate for you. If it's prescribed, they choose your strength.
footer_note: Educational content for Equilibria members. It isn't medical advice. LDN is an off-label use of naltrexone, compounded by a pharmacy and prescribed only after a clinician's review.

figure.figure_alt: Line drawing of a woman. Plum points mark opioid receptors in the brain and spinal cord. Gold dotted rings spread from them to show the theorized rise in the body's own signaling.

story_stops.stop_title: It starts as one small capsule
story_stops.stop_body: LDN is naltrexone at doses studied around {{dose_low_range}} a day. The FDA-approved tablet is {{dose_standard_value}}. No approved low-dose product exists, so a pharmacy compounds your capsules, and your clinician sets the strength.
Naltrexone docks on opioid receptors in the brain and spinal cord, the same receptors your own endorphins use, and blocks them for a while.

story_stops.stop_title: At a low dose, the block is brief
story_stops.stop_body: A standard dose is meant to block around the clock. A low dose is a lighter touch, and researchers think its block lifts within hours. Naltrexone itself has a half-life of about 4 hours.

Once the block lifts, the theory goes, your body makes more of its own endorphins and adds receptors. Over a day, that could mean more of your own signaling, not less. Most support for this comes from animal and cell research.

Naltrexone also appears to quiet TLR4, a receptor on microglia, the resident immune cells of the brain and spinal cord. In lab work this didn't depend on opioid receptors at all. Researchers say the fit isn't perfect yet.

Most LDN studies in people have been small. A 2026 review of 105 studies found it generally well tolerated, but the evidence still lacks strength, and early results from uncontrolled studies rarely held up in placebo-controlled trials. That's why a clinician decides whether it's worth trying for you.
Every member is different. This is what studies have measured, not a promise.

dose_clock.clock_alt: Three rings over one day. The outer ring is fully plum: a standard dose blocks all day. The middle ring is plum for a quarter of the day: a low dose blocks briefly. Gold dots fill the rest of the inner ring: the theorized rebound.

rings.ring_text: Outer ring: the standard {{dose_standard_value}} dose keeps receptors blocked around the clock.
Middle ring: a low dose blocks them for a few hours.
Inner dots: the theorized rise in your own signaling once the block lifts.

dose_clock.clock_caption: An illustration of the idea, not measured data. Doses shown are the label dose and the studied range, not your dose.

crosslink_body: LDN works through one family of receptors. Your endocannabinoid system is another, woven through nearly all of you.
